dnv-trustee-haines-rob.quote:
I have spent more than 23 years in public education, seeing firsthand the difference a great teacher and a strong school can make in the lives of students, families, and communities. I have worked as a secondary teacher, special education teacher, IB educator, and Vice Principal. I've taught in Ontario, Hong Kong, and British Columbia, giving me a broad perspective on education and the needs of students and school communities.

Throughout my career, I have supported students with diverse learning needs, worked to uphold high educational standards, and collaborated with families, educators, and support staff to build strong school communities.

I've spent more than 23 years in public education because I've seen firsthand the difference a great teacher can make. That's what inspired me to become a teacher—the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students, their families, and the communities that support them.​

Throughout my career, I’ve taught in Ontario, Hong Kong, and British Columbia, giving me a broad perspective on different educational systems and approaches to student learning .

My experience includes roles as secondary classroom teacher, primary special education teacher, International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme educator, and Vice Principal. These experiences have allowed me to understand education from multiple perspectives—as a classroom teacher, a specialist supporting students with diverse learning needs, and a school leader working alongside students, families, educators, and support staff.

After more than two decades in education, I’m bringing this experience and perspective to my candidacy for North Vancouver School Trustee.

My experience in special education has shown me the importance of supporting students with diverse needs, while my work in advanced academic programs has reinforced the value of high educational standards and preparing students for future success.

Over my career, I’ve seen the challenges facing public education grow.

Mine began in the financial markets, working at the intersection of economics, investment strategy, and public influence. From managing institutional portfolios to collaborating with regulators, shaping PR and media strategies, and sharing financial insights on television. I spent years in fast-paced, high-impact work shifting systems at an economic level.

It’s about building bridges across cultures, generations, and systems, and using knowledge, access, and experience to open doors for others. ​ For a long time, my world revolved around numbers, managing financial portfolios, markets, performance. I built a successful career in global finance, managing large-scale investments across regions and economies.
Working across both emerging economies and established western systems gave me a front-row seat to how access (or the lack of it) shapes lives.

This inspired me to develop a children’s book designed to help young readers build cultural confidence. I am also working on a second book project focused on financial literacy, introducing basic concepts of money in a developmentally appropriate way and helping children develop essential life skills and healthy financial habits that support long-term success.

​Leaving a successful financial career wasn’t a loss; it was a deliberate choice. I transitioned into leadership development and equity-focused work because I believe real growth happens when systems are designed with people at the center. Today, my work focuses on advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion, empowering women and youth, and supporting responsible funding that creates both impact and sustainability.
My education at Oxford and Yale, and my experience as a Yale World Fellow, sharpened my global perspective but it was lived experience that truly shifted my path.
Today, my work centers on youth, communities, and systems. I focus on building cultural confidence and life skills, creating pathways that ensure everyone has the tools to participate fully. ​

That experience became the catalyst for my community work. I began creating and leading programs focused on cultural confidence, integration, and financial literacy first for adults, then for children. I wanted to start early, to give children the tools I wish more of us had growing up: confidence in who they are, comfort with money, and a sense of agency in the world. Teaching financial literacy from the preschool years onward became one of the most meaningful parts of my work.
Becoming a mother changed the way I understood leadership, resilience, and responsibility. It made equity personal.
Another outcome of this transition took shape while living in Canada, a country with open borders and a welcoming, multicultural environment that aligns closely with my equity initiatives.

I bring over 20 years of experience in governance, financial literacy education, strategic partnerships, and community leadership. Throughout my career, I've worked with governments, educators, nonprofits, and businesses to turn ideas into measurable impact.
As the parent of two children in North Vancouver elementary schools, I care deeply about the environment in which our children learn, grow, and discover their potential.
